facts.text: Bitcoin price predictions for the rest of the year vary widely, with estimates ranging from $40,000 to $80,000.
A Bitcoin price prediction for November suggested that if Bitcoin held above $76,141, it could trade between $76,000 and $82,000, but Bitcoin has since fallen below $76,141.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin would need a 21% rally to hit $80,000 by year-end, but the most probable close sits between $65,000 and $73,000.
Futures price an 89% chance the Fed hikes rates again on December 9, a decision that could swing Bitcoin's year-end path.
However, Bitcoin closed at $58,566 on June 30, just under that call and 11% below it, marking its lowest close in the past year.
However, even in this scenario, Bitcoin would still end the year below its January 1 price of roughly $87,575, which is 33% above its price.
Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most.
His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.
Bitcoin price predictions for the rest of the year vary widely, with estimates ranging from $40,000 to $80,000.
Bitcoin reached $84,082 on October 21 and has dropped 20.4% over the past 30 days, including a 4.3% decline in the last 24 hours.
Research firm Bespoke noted that Bitcoin is “deep into oversold territory,” suggesting that selling pressure might soon ease.
A Bitcoin price prediction for November suggested that if Bitcoin held above $76,141, it could trade between $76,000 and $82,000, but Bitcoin has since fallen below $76,141.
The likelihood of Bitcoin hitting $80,000 by December 31 appears low, with the most probable year-end price between $65,000 and $73,000.
